items.title: 29.5.2 IR Spectra of Important Functional Groups

source_refs.note: Topic 29.5.2 with the note and the second Quick Check 29.2 (the book repeats the number), answered (PDF 193-195). The printed spectra are not reproduced. Answers depend on reading the printed spectra and need review.

items: Alcohols: the O-H group gives a strong, broad absorption at 3200-3600 cm-1 (as in butan-2-ol); the band near 3000 cm-1 is from sp3 C-H bonds.
Amines: an N-H bond gives two weak absorptions near 3300 and 3400 cm-1 (as in octylamine). An N-H signal in an amine is broad, but not broader than the O-H signal of an alcohol.
Amides: absorptions above 1500 cm-1 for both N-H and C=O; N-H (two peaks) near 3200 and 3400 cm-1 and C=O near 1660 cm-1 (as in propanamide).
Carboxylic acids: C=O gives a strong absorption near 1700 cm-1, together with a broad, deep O-H absorption between 2500 and 3300 cm-1, whose right-hand side is often distorted by the C-H peaks.
Of two infrared spectra, which is that of butanone and which is that of butan-2-ol?

Compounds T and U are isomers of C3H6O2. T shows a very broad band from about 2500 to 3300 cm-1 and a strong band near 1700 cm-1; U shows a strong band near 1740 cm-1 and no O-H band. Suggest structures.
